name: absence-claims-need-the-whole-project
description: Before claiming a sibling project lacks a result, search by STATEMENT shape across all its files — finding the weaker cousin in one file and stopping is how a duplicate gets written
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

Claiming "the other project does not have X" requires searching the whole project by the
*shape of the statement*, not by finding a related declaration in the first plausible file.

**Why:** on 2026-07-28 (AJC task `ajc-rr`) I wrote a peel/vanishing-propagation chain into
`RiemannRoch/Ledger/SectionDrop.lean` and documented that the sibling AJCR "has the h1
inequality; it does not have the vanishing propagation." I had searched

stopped. The *propagation* lived in `RiemannRoch/FLVClass.lean` — `peel_single`,

identical variable block, from the identical `surjective_map_f`. I had re-derived it. A

had declared "open at every curve" existed in `FLVVanishing.lean` on the same carrier: I had
measured absence inside my own project's subtree and stated it about the workspace.

**How to apply:** search for the *conclusion pattern* (e.g. `grep -rn "Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule
(X.divisorSheaf K"` across the whole sibling tree) and check whether each hit is a hypothesis or
a conclusion — a hit in binder position means someone assumes it, a hit in conclusion position
means someone proved it. Finding the weaker cousin (an inequality where you want a vanishing) is
positive evidence that the stronger one is nearby, not evidence it is absent. And always name the
cone a negative claim was measured in; see [[cross-project-lean-port-checks]] and
[[subsingleton-not-finrank-for-vanishing]].
